title: Maximum sum of k consecutive values
prompt: Return the largest sum of any k consecutive values in nums (1 <= k <= len(nums)), in O(n).
hints: Start with the sum of the first k values.
Sliding one step adds nums[i] and removes nums[i-k].
Track the best window sum.

title: Shortest subarray with sum at least target
prompt: nums contains positive integers. Return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is >= target, or 0 if none exists.
hints: Grow the window to the right until the sum reaches target.
While it still reaches target, record the length and shrink from the left.
Positivity makes shrinking safe.

title: Longest run with at most k flips
prompt: bits contains 0s and 1s. Return the length of the longest contiguous run of 1s you can get by flipping at most k zeros.
hints: A window is valid while it contains at most k zeros.
Grow right; when zeros exceed k, move left until valid again.
Track the longest valid window.

title: Is a permutation of p inside s?
prompt: Return True if some contiguous substring of s is a rearrangement of p (same letters, same counts).
hints: The window has fixed length len(p).
Compare letter counts of the window with those of p.
Slide: add the entering letter's count, remove the leaving one.

title: Running totals
prompt: Return the list of prefix sums of nums: entry i is nums[0] + … + nums[i].
hints: Keep a running total.
Append it after adding each value.
An empty list gives an empty result.

title: Count subarrays with sum k
prompt: Return how many contiguous non-empty subarrays of nums sum to exactly k. Values may be negative.
hints: A range ending here sums to k iff an earlier prefix equals total − k.
Seed the map with {0: 1}.
Count before recording the current prefix.

title: Pivot index
prompt: Return the leftmost index i where the sum of values strictly left of i equals the sum strictly right of i, or -1.
hints: Compute the total once.
Walk left to right keeping the left sum.
right = total - left - nums[i].

title: Longest balanced binary subarray
prompt: bits contains 0s and 1s. Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray with equally many 0s and 1s.
hints: Treat 0 as -1; a balanced range has sum 0.
Equal prefix sums at two positions mean the range between them is balanced.
Store the first index of each prefix value (prefix 0 at index -1).

title: Merge overlapping intervals
prompt: Merge all overlapping closed intervals [start, end] and return them sorted by start. Intervals that touch (end == next start) merge.
hints: Sort by start first.
If the next interval starts at or before the last merged end, extend it.
Otherwise begin a new merged interval.

title: Minimum meeting rooms
prompt: meetings are half-open [start, end) intervals. Return the minimum number of rooms needed so no two overlapping meetings share a room.
hints: Process meetings by start time.
A min-heap holds the end times of rooms in use.
If the earliest end is <= the new start, reuse that room.

title: LRU cache simulator
prompt: Simulate an LRU cache with the given capacity. ops is a list of ['put', key, value] or ['get', key]. Return the results of every get in order (-1 for a miss). A get refreshes recency.
hints: OrderedDict keeps keys in recency order.
move_to_end(key) on every hit and every put.
After a put, evict with popitem(last=False) if over capacity.

title: Free time across schedules
prompt: busy is a list of half-open [start, end) intervals for one person. Return the gaps (as [start, end]) strictly between busy periods, sorted, after merging overlapping or touching intervals.
hints: Merge first (sort by start).
A gap exists between consecutive merged intervals.
Gap = [previous end, next start] when previous end < next start.

title: Height of a tree
prompt: tree is a nested list [value, left, right] with None for missing children (or tree itself is None). Return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path (0 for an empty tree).
hints: The empty tree has height 0.
A node's height is 1 + the taller child.
Recurse on tree[1] and tree[2].

title: Values by level
prompt: tree is a nested list [value, left, right] (None for missing). Return a list of levels, each a list of values left to right.
hints: Use a queue, starting with the root.
Record the current queue's values as one level.
Then replace the queue with all children of that level.

title: Is it a valid BST?
prompt: tree is a nested list [value, left, right]. Return True if it is a binary search tree with strictly smaller values on the left and strictly larger values on the right of every node.
hints: Each node has an allowed open range (low, high).
Going left lowers high to the node's value; going right raises low.
Start with (-inf, inf).

title: Lowest common ancestor in a BST
prompt: tree is a valid BST as nested lists [value, left, right]; a and b are values present in it. Return the value of their lowest common ancestor in O(height).
hints: If both values are smaller than the node, the LCA is on the left.
If both are larger, go right.
Otherwise the current node splits them: it's the LCA.

title: Next greater element
prompt: For each value, return the next value to its right that is strictly greater, or -1.
hints: Keep indexes of values still waiting for a greater one.
When a larger value arrives, pop and answer them.
Push the current index afterwards.

title: Stock span
prompt: For each day, return the span: the number of consecutive days ending today (including today) with price <= today's price.
hints: Keep indexes of previous prices that are larger than everything after them.
Pop indexes whose price is <= today's.
Span = today's index minus the remaining top (or i + 1 if empty).

title: Largest rectangle in a histogram
prompt: Return the area of the largest rectangle that fits under the histogram heights (bars of width 1).
hints: Keep indexes of increasing heights on a stack.
When a lower bar arrives, popped bars can't extend further right: measure them.
Width = i − (new top) − 1, or i if the stack is empty; add a 0 sentinel at the end.

title: Remove k digits
prompt: num is a string of digits. Remove exactly k digits to make the smallest possible number; return it without leading zeros ('0' if nothing is left).
hints: A digit should go if a smaller digit follows it.
Keep an increasing stack; pop while the top is larger and removals remain.
Remove leftover k from the end, then strip leading zeros.

title: First true in a monotone predicate
prompt: flags is a list of booleans that is all False then all True. Return the index of the first True, or len(flags) if there is none, in O(log n).
hints: Search in [0, len(flags)].
If flags[mid] is True, the answer is at mid or left of it.
Otherwise it's right of mid.

title: Ship within d days
prompt: Packages with the given weights must ship in order, at most one day's capacity per day. Return the smallest daily capacity that ships everything within days days.
hints: Feasibility: greedily fill days without exceeding capacity.
The answer lies between max(weights) and sum(weights).
Find the first capacity that is feasible.

title: Minimum eating speed
prompt: piles[i] bananas; you eat at speed s per hour, one pile per hour at most (an hour with fewer than s left finishes that pile). Return the minimum integer s to finish within h hours (h >= len(piles)).
hints: Hours at speed s = sum(ceil(p / s)).
Faster speed never needs more hours: monotone.
Search s in [1, max(piles)]; ceil(p/s) = (p + s - 1) // s.

title: Split into k parts minimising the largest sum
prompt: Split nums (non-negative) into k non-empty contiguous parts (1 <= k <= len(nums)) to minimise the largest part sum. Return that minimum.
hints: Guess a limit; check whether nums can be cut into <= k parts with sums <= limit.
Feasibility is monotone in the limit.
Search the limit in [max(nums), sum(nums)].

title: Sum of all values
prompt: tree is a nested list [value, left, right] or None. Return the sum of all values (0 for an empty tree).
hints: Empty tree sums to 0.
A node's sum = its value + the sums of both subtrees.
Recurse into tree[1] and tree[2].

title: Inorder traversal without recursion
prompt: Return the inorder (left, node, right) sequence of values of the nested-list tree, using an explicit stack.
hints: Push nodes while walking left.
Pop one, record it, then move to its right child.
Loop while the stack or the current node is non-empty.

title: Diameter of a tree
prompt: Return the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes of the nested-list tree (0 for empty or single-node trees).
hints: The longest path through a node uses the heights of both children.
Compute heights bottom-up and update a best value at each node.
Return the best, counting edges.

title: Root-to-leaf path sums
prompt: Return True if some root-to-leaf path in the nested-list tree has values summing to target. An empty tree has no paths.
hints: Pass the remaining target down the tree.
At a leaf, check whether the remainder equals its value.
A node with one child is not a leaf.

title: Kth largest
prompt: Return the kth largest value in nums (counting duplicates; 1 <= k <= len(nums)) using a min-heap of size k.
hints: Keep the k largest seen so far in a min-heap.
When the heap grows past k, pop its smallest.
At the end, heap[0] is the kth largest.

title: Last stone weight
prompt: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones: equal stones both vanish, otherwise the lighter vanishes and the heavier loses the lighter's weight. Return the last stone's weight, or 0.
hints: You need the two largest repeatedly: a max-heap.
heapq is a min-heap, so store negatives.
Push back the difference if it's non-zero.

title: Merge k sorted lists
prompt: Merge the sorted lists into one sorted list in O(N log k) using a heap of the current list heads.
hints: Start the heap with (first value, list index, position) for each non-empty list.
Pop the smallest, then push the next element of that list.
The index in the tuple breaks ties.

title: K closest points
prompt: Return the k points [x, y] closest to the origin (by squared distance), sorted by distance, ties broken by x then y.
hints: Squared distance avoids square roots.
heapq.nsmallest with a key does the selection in O(n log k).
Key: (x*x + y*y, x, y).

title: Most non-overlapping meetings
prompt: Return the maximum number of pairwise non-overlapping half-open intervals [start, end) you can choose.
hints: Sort by end time.
Take an interval if it starts at or after the last chosen end.
Count what you take.

title: Assign cookies
prompt: Child i is content with a cookie of size >= greed[i]. Each child gets at most one cookie. Return the maximum number of content children.
hints: Sort both lists.
Give the smallest adequate cookie to the least greedy child.
Advance through cookies; advance the child pointer only on success.

title: Jump game
prompt: nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i. Return True if you can reach the last index starting from index 0 (an empty list counts as False).
hints: Track the farthest index reachable so far.
If you reach an index beyond that frontier, you're stuck.
Update farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]).

title: Does greedy coin change fail?
prompt: Return the smallest amount between 1 and limit for which taking the largest coin first uses more coins than the optimum, or -1 if greedy is optimal for every amount up to limit. coins always contains 1.
hints: Compute the optimal coin counts with DP up to limit.
Simulate greedy for each amount.
Return the first amount where greedy > optimal.

title: Longest common prefix
prompt: Return the longest common prefix of all strings in words ('' for an empty list).
hints: Compare character columns of the first word with the others.
Stop at the first mismatch or the end of any word.
Return the first word up to that column.

title: Trie: which queries are prefixes?
prompt: Insert every word into a trie (nested dicts), then return a list of booleans: for each query, whether some word starts with it.
hints: Insert: walk/create one dict per character.
Query: walk; if a character is missing, it's not a prefix.
The empty query is a prefix of everything (if any words exist? here: always True).

title: Autocomplete top three
prompt: For each prefix of query (query[:1], query[:2], …), return up to three words from words that start with it, in lexicographic order.
hints: Sorting words once makes matches contiguous.
For each prefix, find the first word >= prefix with bisect.
Take up to three consecutive words that start with the prefix.

title: Replace words with roots
prompt: Replace every word in sentence with the shortest root from roots that is a prefix of it (keep the word if none). Return the new sentence.
hints: Put the roots in a trie with end markers.
For each word, walk the trie and stop at the first end marker.
If the walk fails before any marker, keep the word.

title: All subsets
prompt: Return every subset of the distinct values in nums, generated by deciding exclude-then-include for each value in order.
hints: At index i, first recurse without nums[i], then with it.
Record a copy of the current subset at the end.
Pop after the include branch.

title: Combinations of size k
prompt: Return all combinations of k numbers chosen from 1..n, each in increasing order, listed in lexicographic order.
hints: Choose numbers in increasing order with a start value.
Stop when the combination has k numbers.
Recurse with start = chosen + 1.

title: Subsets without duplicates
prompt: nums may contain duplicates. Return all distinct subsets, each sorted ascending, with the list of subsets sorted lexicographically.
hints: Sort nums first.
At each depth, skip a value equal to the previous one at the same depth.
Sort the final list to fix the order.

title: Count N-queens solutions
prompt: Return the number of ways to place n queens on an n×n board so that none attack each other.
hints: Place one queen per row.
Track used columns and both diagonals (r - c and r + c) in sets.
Undo the three markers after each recursive call.

title: Pick the technique
prompt: Given flags describing a subarray-sum problem, return 'sliding window' if all values are positive, 'prefix sums' if values may be negative, and 'brute force' if n <= 50 regardless.
hints: Tiny inputs don't need cleverness.
Positive values make shrinking a window safe.
Otherwise prefix sums with a hash map.

title: Feasible complexity for n
prompt: Return the slowest complexity class among ['O(n^2)', 'O(n log n)', 'O(n)'] whose operation count stays at or under 10**8 for the given n (use n*n, n*log2(n), n). If none fit, return 'too large'.
hints: Check the slowest class first.
math.log2(n) gives log base 2; treat n <= 1 as log 1.
Return the first class whose count is <= 10**8.

title: Two sum: sorted or not?
prompt: Return [i, j] (i < j, original indexes) of two values summing to target, or []. If several pairs exist return the one with the smallest j, then smallest i. Must work for unsorted input.
hints: Unsorted input rules out two pointers without losing indexes.
A map from value to its first index finds the complement.
Scanning j left to right finds the smallest j first.

title: Count ranges with sum k (any sign)
prompt: Return how many contiguous non-empty subarrays of nums sum to k. Values may be negative or zero.
hints: Negative values rule out a sliding window.
Count earlier prefix sums equal to current − k.
Seed with {0: 1}.
